title: Lrp5 functions in bone to regulate bone mass
authors: Cui Y, Niziolek PJ, MacDonald BT, Zylstra CR, Alenina N, Robinson DR, et al.
population: Mice with inducible bone-cell or intestinal Lrp5 mutations, Tph1-null mice, and intact or ovariectomised mice and rats treated with the Tph1 inhibitor LP-923941
funder: NIH grants AR53237, GM74241 and AR053293, a PHS Career Development Award, a Leukemia and Lymphoma Society Scholarship, the Van Andel Research Institute and the Howard Hughes Medical Institute. Eight authors were employees of Lexicon Pharmaceuticals and Merck Sharp & Dohme Research Laboratories with salary and stock options.
result: Lrp5 acted locally in osteocytes; Lrp5 genotype was not associated with blood serotonin; bone mass of Tph1-null mice did not differ significantly from wild type after correction for multiple testing; a Tph1 inhibitor that lowered whole-blood serotonin by 42% to 44% for 6 weeks without changing brain serotonin did not reproduce the bone gain reported earlier. Animal data contradicting the gut serotonin model of Yadav and colleagues.
